answers.limitations: Registered scripts bind frozen claim text and source/quote selectors only to actually admitted evidence; missing selectors abstain. This measures software and retrieval, not learned generation quality. Five rows use one explicitly fictional Harbour District profile, registered before scoring; the shipped Hong Kong profile and original corpus facts are unchanged. The hypothesis row orders admitted context using the pre-existing 0.6/1.3/0.05 weights, never eligibility. Optimizer plans use the original atomic question. Separate contract/retrieval/web components retain their earlier profile and registration.

flow.correction: The earlier component script classified stages using any message, including quoted user content. Matching the system message fixes 29 assessment requests per web-enabled row. Claim scores and physical call counts are unchanged; each corrected row records 290 more tokens. The earlier receipt is frozen in the flow registration.
flow.limitations: Registered scripts and exact replay test orchestration, cost accounting and evidence visibility. They do not establish live model quality. The frozen earlier component receipt is retained separately from any instrument correction.

Equivalence control: the registered full treatment already uses these historical weights. No newly optimized ordering or independent improvement is claimed.

suites.predicate: No visible claim or citation survives a URL outside the retained evidence registry.

Two conflicting official sources under critical policy cause refusal with no visible claim and retained rule provenance.
The emergency rule routes the entire request before any model or web request.
A fact supplied to a separate conversation cannot enter this conversation plan or visible answer through a scripted resolution proposal.
Both registered diagnosis and dosage requests take their exact out-of-scope rule with zero model or web requests.
An empty curated corpus plus a discovery-only web response cannot produce a positive claim or visible citation.
